title: Texas Form 2703: franchise exemption notice before offering

sections.heading: The condition and prior filing are separate
paragraphs: The Secretary of State’s FAQ describes material compliance in Texas with applicable Federal Trade Commission disclosure requirements and prohibitions as the franchise exemption condition. It also requires the notice before the covered offer or sale.

Form 2703 asks for the franchisor’s legal name, every name under which it does or intends to do business, and principal business address. The FAQ lists $25 and describes a one-time notice without expiry, with principal-address changes notified in writing.
A completed Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) or a “licence” contract heading does not establish the actual exemption and notice conditions. No expiry does not guarantee continued eligibility.

title: New York franchise sales: registration and disclosure timing

paragraphs: The Attorney General says offerings in or from New York must be registered before offer or sale unless exempt. General Business Law (GBL) 681(3) has alternative branches: a substantially prescribed marketing plan plus a required direct or indirect fee, OR substantial brand association plus that fee. Both plan and brand elements are not required in every arrangement.

Fee exclusions, area/subfranchise roles, uninterrupted renewals and state connections also matter. Part 200.1 adds fee and advice/training meanings. The actual rights, payments, support, offer/acceptance locations and proposed operation determine which branch or exemption needs examination.

sections.heading: Use the earliest applicable buyer event
paragraphs: GBL 683(8) requires the offering prospectus—the seller’s required buyer-disclosure information—and proposed agreements at the earliest applicable event below. Consideration means the relevant money or other value. The statute and the currently linked agency addendum use different day wording; that difference is not resolved here.

rows: The defined first face-to-face meeting to discuss a sale or possible franchise sale is an independent trigger.
GBL 683(8): binding franchise or other agreement
At least ten business days before the agreement.
At least ten days before receipt; the statute does not say business days here.
Uses ten business days alongside execution or related payment.
Fourteen calendar days where it applies; this does not remove an earlier state meeting or payment trigger.

sections.heading: Renewal, changed information and advertising
paragraphs: The agency guide directs annual renewal within 120 days after the franchisor’s fiscal year end. A fiscal year is its accounting year. The guide distinguishes timely pending renewal from expired registration: after expiry, no covered offers or sales within or from New York until renewal is submitted and accepted for filing.
The renewal package includes an updated Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), marked changes, accountant consent, franchise-sales information, prices, credit terms and audited financial statements.

Part 200.5 separately requires prompt notification by an application to amend material prospectus changes, including the stated fee, significant adverse business/obligation/agreement/product or model, and financial changes. Do not wait for annual renewal.

The agency guide requires two advertising copies through FRED, the North American Securities Administrators Association’s franchise filing system, at least seven days before intended use. The advertising companion explains that separate submission.

sections.heading: Read waivers and side documents too
paragraphs: GBL 687(4)–(5) addresses waiver of statutory compliance and required releases, assignments, novations, waivers or estoppels relieving statutory duty or liability. These can surrender, transfer, replace or prevent assertion of rights; the signing context and exact wording matter. The provisions do not decide every later negotiated settlement.
The addendum also addresses preserved renewal/transfer rights, choice clauses and the stated limits on claim-waiver or reliance-disclaimer effects in commencement questionnaires and acknowledgments.

practicalOutput: Before scheduling the first sales meeting or accepting money, establish registration/exemption status and resolve the applicable delivery dates, including the statute/addendum difference.
limitations: The ten-day versus ten-business-day payment wording is preserved, not resolved.
Coverage, exemptions and state connections depend on the actual offer; this is not a complete operating-law review.
learningSummary: A New York franchise sale can require registration and disclosure before the first sales meeting. Annual renewal is a separate duty; it does not replace buyer delivery, prompt amendments or advertising submission.

title: Oregon franchise sales: disclosure without prior filing approval
description: Understand the state definition, fourteen-day delivery rule and sale records before treating the absence of a filing process as clearance.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Check the arrangement and Oregon connections
paragraphs: The Division of Financial Regulation (DFR) points to ORS Chapter 650 and OAR Chapter 441, Division 325, complaint handling and a conditional private civil remedy.

The reviewed 2025 ORS 650.005 uses marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration elements. Its franchisor definition includes a subfranchisor selling a franchise for $100 or more to a franchisee/subfranchisor; this is not a universal conclusion about low-fee arrangements.
Section 650.015 examines offer origin/direction, acceptance and stated domicile/operation facts. An outlet address alone does not settle those connections.

sections.heading: Deliver all proposed agreements in time
paragraphs: OAR 441-325-0020 requires disclosure and all proposed sale agreements at least fourteen calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration, including refundable deposits.
Unchanged renewals, additional units and owner resales have distinct exception conditions. An existing buyer is not automatically excepted; the linked transaction guide explains those branches.

sections.heading: Retain the sale and proceeds details
paragraphs: DFR identifies complete books, records and franchise-sale details, including distribution of proceeds. The actual delivered documents, recipient/date, signed terms and money received help connect those required records to the sale; an unexplained bank total is not the whole record.

practicalOutput: Before an agreement or refundable deposit, establish coverage or the exact exception and deliver the complete package on time.
limitations: Based on the stated 2025 official statute and administrative rules, not every distribution, licensing or sector regime. Actual state connections and exceptions remain necessary; the civil remedy is not a predicted outcome.

title: Wisconsin franchise registration: a receipt does not certify the business
description: Understand registration on receipt, the separate buyer-disclosure period and annual or material-event filing tasks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Receipt does not replace earlier buyer delivery
paragraphs: The Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) says registration is required no later than the first Wisconsin franchise sale and is effective on receipt. It does not evaluate the opportunity’s merits.

Separately, give the Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) fourteen calendar days before the earlier binding franchise or other agreement or payment. A same-day registration receipt does not show that a buyer received the correct package two weeks earlier.

sections.heading: An amendment does not restart the registration year
paragraphs: DFI lists $400 registration and one-year effectiveness, with separate filing for each system. Two service systems in one group therefore need their respective filings.

The agency lists material-event amendments within 30 days and $200. A corporate reorganization needs assessment as the actual possible event; waiting for annual renewal is not the stated amendment process. An amendment does not reset the year. Recheck current fees before payment.

sections.heading: Operating protections have an independent test
paragraphs: Chapter 135’s dealership/community-of-interest inquiry is separate from registration and federal fee analysis. The linked Fair Dealership Law guide explains cause, notice/cure and marked inventory, including why ten-day nonpayment cure is not automatic day-11 termination.

practicalOutput: Keep each system registered and deliver the correct buyer package early enough; address material events without waiting for renewal.
limitations: Actual system scope, offers and exemptions need application. Registration does not decide Fair Dealership Law coverage or approve the transaction.

title: Minnesota franchise registration and buyer disclosure
description: Use the effective order, seven-day state buyer package and separate federal period. Actual financial-assurance conditions can also restrict initial fees.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: An application is not effective registration
paragraphs: Section 80C.01 subdivision 4 includes a route involving brand rights, a shared commercial interest (community of interest), and a direct or indirect fee and other branches for fuel, specified business-opportunity promises and certain security-system payments. Area franchises, fee definitions/exclusions and wholesale or fair-market-value treatment need their own conditions; the federal control-or-assistance test is not a substitute.

Under sections 80C.02–.03, covered offers/sales require effective registration unless the franchise or transaction is exempt. The Department directs filings through ComOnline. Section 80C.08 gives 12 months from the Commissioner’s order, with the prescribed annual report before that period ends.

sections.heading: Deliver the buyer’s package under both applicable rules
paragraphs: For a franchise subject to state registration requirements, section 80C.06 subdivision 5 and agency guidance require the current public offering statement and all proposed agreements at least seven days before the earlier execution of a franchise or other agreement or payment of consideration—money or other value.

Obtain the signed acknowledgement before agreement/payment and retain it for three years from taking it. The independent federal 14-calendar-day requirement applies where covered; seven state days do not shorten it.

sections.heading: A signed sale may not release its initial fee
paragraphs: Where adequate financial arrangements have not been demonstrated, the Commissioner may require escrow, impoundment or fee deferral; guidance also describes a surety-bond alternative and deferral until the operator opens. These are possible actual-review conditions, not universal restrictions. Escrow or impoundment holds the funds under specified conditions; deferral postpones collection or availability. A surety bond is a guarantee from a surety company under its stated terms.

If the fee is unavailable until opening, it cannot fund earlier training or travel without another usable source. The support-funding companion explains that cash gap. Read the actual condition and release terms.
Registration expiry does not decide contract renewal, termination or transfer; the separate relationship guide addresses those actions.

practicalOutput: Establish registration or exemption before a covered offer, then schedule buyer delivery and check any actual fee-release condition.
limitations: Actual fee exclusions, sector exceptions, exemptions and financial conditions are not determined here. Agreement changes and delivery facts also need application to the transaction.
learningSummary: A covered Minnesota offer or sale needs effective registration unless exempt. Use the Commissioner’s actual order for the registration period, and treat buyer delivery and any restriction on initial fees as separate requirements.

title: Hawaii franchise filing errors: seller names and financial statements
description: Avoid mismatched seller, funding and accountant-consent details. Statement-age rules and complete offer timing are not established here.

sections.heading: Submit the right package for the actual seller
paragraphs: Hawaii’s Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs (DCCA) directs franchise filings to the Securities Online Portal. Its tips call for the required materials together under the relevant initial, renewal or amendment category, with the associated fee.

If a U.S. subsidiary will sell the franchises, its application, Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), agreements, seller information, costs and source-of-funds material must describe that arrangement. A parent’s accounts or name do not establish a commitment to fund the subsidiary’s promises.

For example, Form B showing parent-company costs and accountant consent referring to a different statement set need correction against the actual seller, obligations, funding company and accounting periods. Any proposed parent guarantee must name the right parties and statements.

sections.heading: Check consents and overseas signatures
paragraphs: The tips call for Form C to be notarized by a U.S. notary. They also call for signed, dated accountant consent from a qualified certified public accounting (CPA) firm, referring to the correct statements and relevant guarantor statements where applicable.
Confirm the currently accepted notarization process before arranging signatures abroad; an ordinary signature is not necessarily equivalent.

sections.heading: The 120-day position does not settle offer timing
paragraphs: DCCA currently links Interpretive Order 2023-1, dated April 19, 2023. It describes the underlying 90-day financial-statement requirement and says the Commissioner will take no action to require 90-day currency if the statements are current within 120 days of the registration application. It remains effective until amended or rescinded by another interpretive order or rule. This is the stated no-action position, not a claim that every financial-statement condition has been removed.

The agency’s fee table lists $250 each for franchise initial filing, amendment and renewal. Those fees and the statement-age position do not establish when a covered offer may begin or what buyer delivery requires.

practicalOutput: Correct seller and statement mismatches, then confirm current execution, statement-age and offer-timing requirements before relying on the filing.
limitations: Limited to filing preparation, the cited fee table and Order 2023-1’s conditional no-action position. Complete registration/effectiveness, buyer-disclosure, exemption and current execution requirements remain unresolved.
learningSummary: Hawaii’s filing instructions require the seller’s names, financial statements, funding information and consents to describe the same offering. This page addresses those filing errors; it does not establish when an offer may begin.

title: Maryland: an exemption may still require disclosure before the first meeting
description: Select the exact route, then plan buyer documents, notices, advertising and registration dates separately.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Registration relief is not relief from every duty
paragraphs: Business Regulation section 14-201 includes express/implied, oral/written arrangements with a substantially prescribed marketing plan/system, substantial brand association and a direct or indirect fee, including area franchises. Goods/services payments can count, subject to specified wholesale, fair-market-value and other exclusions.

Section 14-214 requires registration before covered offers, including advertising, or sales unless excluded or exempt. COMAR 02.02.08.10 has particular exemption routes. For D–G, absent a contrary order, deliver the offering circular and proposed agreements at the earlier of the first personal meeting or ten business days before signing/payment; specified routes also have notice conditions.

The regulation uses older Uniform Franchise Offering Circular terminology. A newer Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) name does not remove its earlier meeting trigger. The independent federal period must also be met. Moving a Belgian prospect’s payment later would not remove an applicable first-meeting condition.

sections.heading: If registration is required, these are different events
paragraphs: Use the actual route and order conditions; these are not one universal timetable.

rows: Absent a stop order, noon on the thirtieth business day after the application or last amendment filing, or earlier Commissioner-set time. A filing receipt is not itself effectiveness.
Normally the first-anniversary regime, with materials at least 15 business days before expiry, subject to order and other conditions.
Prompt amendment; if approved, the Commissioner sets its effective date. No fixed 30-day allowance is supplied.
For an offering subject to registration, submit covered advertising at least five days before anticipated initial use.

sections.heading: Check sale-conditioned waivers separately
paragraphs: Section 14-226 bars requiring specified release, assignment, novation, waiver or estoppel arrangements relieving a person of statutory liability as a condition of sale. These can surrender, transfer, replace or prevent assertion of rights. The provision does not decide every later settlement, termination or choice-of-law issue.

practicalOutput: Before a personal sales meeting, identify the precise exemption or effective registration route and the documents and notice it requires.
limitations: Exact exemption, fee exclusions, orders and current agency instructions need application to the offer. The legacy meeting trigger is preserved; the waiver rule is limited to its stated sale condition.

title: South Dakota franchises: notice, disclosure and financial events need separate dates

paragraphs: SDCL 37-5B-4 requires a covered offer/sale to be properly notice filed or exempt. Section 5’s package contains the Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), application, consent to service and $250 initial fee.

paragraphs: Use actual exemptions, versions and changed signing terms, not one generic waiting period.

reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the actual seller’s current notice route
paragraphs: KRS 367.807(1)(a) links the exemption to the federal franchise definition, federal compliance and written notice. Current 40 KAR 12:410, effective June 30, 2026, directs section 3 notices through the Franchise Exemption Notice portal with authority-to-transact evidence and the offeror’s Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD).

Match the seller in the offer, authority evidence and FDD. A parent’s history does not establish a subsidiary’s authority. Older/redline material and former determination forms are not automatically the current process; registration, renewal and exempt-offeror routes differ.

sections.heading: Fourteen days does not override an immediate statutory duty
paragraphs: Current rule section 4 requires written notification within fourteen days of material changes by stated registered sellers and exempt-notice offerors. KRS 367.805(2) separately says a registered offeror shall notify immediately.
Preserve both instructions and apply the actual route. The regulation is not permission for a registered seller to delay an immediate statutory duty or wait for annual paperwork.

sections.heading: The nonexempt process is separate
paragraphs: For a covered seller without an established exemption, the rule requires approval before covered sales to Kentucky residents, electronic registration/renewal and supporting documents. This route has its own fees; approved registration/renewal lasts one year from written confirmation.

Its cancellation wording remains unreconciled: KRS 367.816’s prescribed notice says thirty business days, while 367.819 says thirty calendar days. Do not turn either into a single resolved deadline or apply the provisions automatically to an established franchise exemption.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying route, use the current seller’s portal documents and apply the appropriate notification rule when facts change.
limitations: Exemption eligibility and the nonexempt cancellation conflict are not resolved. A portal record does not establish advertising, relationship or industry-law compliance.
learningSummary: Kentucky’s qualifying franchise-exemption route uses the current notice portal and the actual offeror’s documents. Important changes need separate notification; a completed notice is not the end of the duty.
seoTitle: Kentucky Franchise Exemption Portal and Material Changes

title: Louisiana business opportunities: sales promises, trademark wording and bonds
description: A registered mark does not settle separate device-location, buyback or earnings triggers. Bonds and written promises need their own checks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Test the buyback or income promise separately
paragraphs: RS 51:1821 puts registered-mark wording within the specified sales/marketing-plan branch. Specified device-location help, product buyback and earnings/refund representations have separate conditions. Device placement is not every form of customer-finding or site advice.

For example, a German seller promising to buy back output if the operator is dissatisfied must test that promise separately from its registered mark. The actual payments and other conditions still matter.

sections.heading: When the bond requirement applies
paragraphs: RS 51:1822 requires covered bonds before conducting business, including advertising or soliciting. Subsections A and B require authorized-surety bond face amounts of $50,000 for a covered seller and $25,000 for a covered agent, including the stated independent contractor, broker or employee roles. These are bond amounts, not a quoted premium or application fee; the actual role matters. Subsection G limits the bond duty to opportunities defined in 1821(1)(a), (b) or (c), not every trademark licence.

For those opportunities, subsection H makes the bond continuous. The surety—the company guaranteeing the bond—can terminate through 60 days’ written notice to the specified assistant secretary and the principal, whose obligations the bond guarantees; liability continues during that period and for accrued pre-termination liability discovered later. Subsection E requires a new/additional bond before continuing business. The 60 days is a bond rule, not franchise-contract exit notice.

sections.heading: The agreement must reflect covered oral promises
paragraphs: For covered opportunities, RS 51:1823 addresses documented earnings support, specified ad disclosures, actual seller identification and appointment of the secretary of state for service of process.

Subsection (6) requires the written agreement to include material oral statements, representations and promises made before execution. Subsection (7) prohibits waiver of purchaser legal rights; signing does not erase the earlier sales conversation.

sections.heading: A separate rule applies to real-estate brokerage
paragraphs: RS 37:1465 prohibits the described franchisor from contracting with a Louisiana real-estate broker without appointing a Louisiana-licensed broker as state representative. Property maintenance is not automatically brokerage.

practicalOutput: Test the actual promises and seller/agent roles before advertising, then arrange any applicable bond and confirm its filing procedure.
limitations: Actual coverage, role and bond procedure require application. The stated bond face amounts do not quote an insurance premium; the limited bond and brokerage rules are not complete franchise or operating-law treatment.
learningSummary: A registered brand does not automatically exclude an equipment-and-buyback package from Louisiana’s business-opportunity rules. The actual promise determines which definition branch—and possible pre-promotion bond duty—needs examination.
seoTitle: Louisiana Business Opportunities: Promises and Bond Duties

title: Maine business opportunities: promotion, first meetings and buyer disclosure
description: Covered business opportunities have early promotion and disclosure duties, followed by cancellation, security and renewal tasks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the actual package
paragraphs: Title 32, Chapter 69-B addresses specified location assistance, buyback, earnings/refund promises and marketing assistance, subject to its wording and exceptions. The federally registered-mark qualification belongs to the marketing-program branch, not every other trigger.
An equipment-and-training offer with an independent buyback promise needs that separate coverage analysis before using the covered timetable.

sections.heading: Match the duty to its earliest event
paragraphs: The state timetable is independent of federal franchise disclosure.

rows: Section 4692 uses the earliest specified 72-hour pre-agreement/pre-payment event or first face-to-face sales meeting. Calling a relevant sales meeting informal does not remove the trigger.

Section 4698 allows the buyer to withdraw by written notice within three full business days following the contract day, with its goods/funds return provisions. Signature does not make all receipts irreversible.
Sections 4695–4697 have applicable security, registration and exception conditions; do not assume every seller needs the same arrangement.
Update the disclosure statement as material information changes under 4696; annual renewal is not the only update.
Section 4697: one year from effectiveness. Renewal needs current disclosure, required fee and qualifying security evidence; failure to renew expires registration.

practicalOutput: Check coverage before promoting, then compare the first sales meeting with the agreement/payment disclosure triggers.
limitations: The official PDF is current through October 1, 2026 and is not the officially certified annotated text. Current forms, certified wording and case-specific interpretation may need confirmation.
Exact coverage, exceptions and all return obligations are not determined here.
learningSummary: For a covered Maine business opportunity, registration can be required before promotion and buyer disclosure can be due at the first face-to-face sales meeting. Waiting until signature can therefore be too late.

title: Massachusetts contractor status: why choosing hours is not enough
description: The statute requires an individual-services analysis and all three contractor conditions. A franchise label does not answer it.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify whose services and alleged employer are at issue
paragraphs: Chapter 149, section 148B starts with an individual performing services. Apply that threshold to the actual relationship and relevant current cases before moving to the exception. A brand, operator company, owner and technician do not all acquire one status together.

A technician choosing a schedule and a brand remotely checking quality are relevant facts, not a finished classification. Compare contractual controls with actual instructions, supervision, payment and the customer-contract/invoice roles. A franchise or contractor label proves neither universal employee nor contractor status.

sections.heading: All three conditions must be satisfied
paragraphs: Once the services threshold applies, the contractor exception requires all three: the individual is free from control and direction under the contract and in fact; the service is outside the alleged employer’s usual course of business; and the individual is customarily engaged in an independently established trade, occupation, profession or business of the same nature as the service performed.
Choosing hours alone addresses neither the whole control inquiry nor the other two conditions. This framework does not resolve current franchise-specific case application.

practicalOutput: Identify the individual’s service and possible employer, then examine every applicable condition rather than relying on schedule choice or a contract label.
limitations: The services threshold and relevant current cases require application to the actual facts. This is not a franchisee/technician classification verdict, and other employment or tax tests remain separate.
learningSummary: Letting a Massachusetts technician choose their hours does not establish independent-contractor status. After the individual-services threshold is met, section 148B requires all three contractor conditions—not a favourable answer to only one.
seoTitle: Massachusetts contractor status: why choosing hours is not enough

title: Missouri: document territory promises and review exit notice separately
description: Recruitment representations and an existing operator’s exit use different definitions and legal tests.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Do the exclusive customer promises overlap?
paragraphs: Sections 409.1000 and 409.1003 have a business-opportunity definition/exclusions separate from the relationship law. For covered offers, prohibited practices include the specified investment, training/support, profit and contract-rights representations and assigning the same “exclusive” territory to multiple purchasers.

A Belgian brand retaining national accounts inside two local territories must describe which customers and rights each promise includes. A private map not explained in the pitch does not cure conflicting promises. Covered sellers must provide a written contract and not misrepresent termination, transfer or renewal provisions.

sections.heading: A later exit uses its own coverage and exceptions
paragraphs: Section 407.400 uses a definition involving a licence and shared commercial interest (community of interest), Missouri place-of-business condition and specific exclusions. If covered, section 407.405 generally requires at least ninety days’ written notice of cancellation, termination or nonrenewal.
Specified misconduct, abandonment, insolvency and bad-check exceptions need their actual conditions; alleging default alone does not establish an exception.

sections.heading: Do not borrow a neighbouring remedy
paragraphs: Section 407.410(1)’s double-consideration and attorney-fee wording concerns inducing participation in a pyramid sales scheme, not an ordinary franchise notice dispute.

Subsection (2) separately allows a franchisee harmed by missing required cancellation or termination notice to seek the listed damages, including lost reputation/customer value (goodwill), costs and appropriate court orders directing or preventing conduct. The loss must be connected to the missing notice. Coverage, the actual notice failure and actual loss still need proof; this page establishes no award or complete court application.

practicalOutput: Make the actual territory promises consistent before offering; use the separate relationship test before later relying on an exit exception.
limitations: This establishes neither a universal state disclosure period nor absence of registration. Actual coverage, exemptions, notice exceptions and full judicial remedies remain unresolved.
learningSummary: Promising a territory and later ending an operator’s rights raise different Missouri rules. Accurate territory wording does not create immediate-exit rights, and the two laws have separate definitions.

title: Montana construction-equipment dealers: exit rules and separate stock repurchase
description: Construction-equipment dealer protections and inventory repurchase rules require separate coverage and evidence checks.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Part 9 is about a defined equipment relationship
paragraphs: MCA 30-11-901 includes oral/written and express/implied arrangements with a shared commercial interest (community of interest) in construction-equipment distribution. Separate equipment rights, retail/wholesale roles and branded services; a service-agreement heading is not the full definition.

sections.heading: Cause does not replace the notice branch
paragraphs: Under 30-11-902, the grantor—the party granting dealership rights, such as the supplier—must establish good cause for covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal or substantial competitive changes and bears the proof burden. A contract clause or missed target does not itself establish it.

Section 903 generally requires 90 days’ prior notice by certified mail and 60 days to rectify deficiencies. Nonpayment has its own ten-day notice/remedy rule. Specified insolvency, assignment-for-creditors and bankruptcy grounds have different notice treatment under subsections (2)–(3). An alleged financial difficulty is not automatically a listed event.

sections.heading: Part 7 is a separate inventory test
paragraphs: Part 7 has distinct definitions for inventory repurchase, including industrial/construction equipment and repair parts. Part 9 coverage does not establish every Part 7 condition.

Apply the qualifying contract, condition, price basis and exclusions to the actual items, using age, invoices, freight, title and condition evidence. The spreadsheet’s full value is not a proved recovery.

practicalOutput: Identify the covered relationship and actual action before choosing a notice branch; assess any stock repurchase independently.
limitations: Part 9 and Part 7 have separate scopes. General franchise and business-opportunity sales requirements remain unresolved; no actual cause, exception or inventory value is determined.
learningSummary: For a covered Montana construction-equipment dealership, a missed sales target alone does not settle whether quick replacement is permitted. Good cause, notice and correction are separate requirements; inventory repurchase has a separate scope.

title: Nebraska recruitment: qualifying franchise notice versus SAMP filing
description: Understand the difference between a qualifying franchise notice and the separate seller-assisted marketing-plan process.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The qualifying franchise route
paragraphs: Section 59-1722’s conditional exemption from the Seller-Assisted Marketing Plans (SAMP) Act incorporates specified federal provisions as they existed January 1, 2026. A completed disclosure document or licence label alone does not establish those conditions.

The statute requires notice and a $100 fee before specified Nebraska-based advertising, offers or representations to Nebraska prospects. The notice identifies the actual seller, contacts, operating name and plan. Some prohibitions remain despite exemption.

The regulator describes this as a one-time notice without renewal, distinguishing contact-only amendments from other changes. One time does not mean every later change is irrelevant. Acknowledgement is not approval or verification of profit claims.

sections.heading: The covered nonexempt route is different
paragraphs: Section 59-1724 requires prior disclosure filing and $100 fee, material-change filings and annual updates for a covered nonexempt SAMP.

Section 59-1732 addresses disclosure at the first specified in-person or written communication and at least 48 hours before the relevant contract or consideration. These duties do not shorten independently applicable federal disclosure.

practicalOutput: Choose the actual route before the recruitment campaign, using the seller, message and Nebraska connections rather than signing day alone.
limitations: Limited to the stated filing and disclosure branches, not every Nebraska sales, relationship or operating duty.
learningSummary: Nebraska’s qualifying franchise exemption can still require a $100 notice before specified recruitment activity. If that exemption is not established, the nonexempt seller-assisted marketing plan route has different filing and buyer-delivery duties.
seoTitle: Nebraska Franchise Notice vs SAMP Filing

title: Nevada farm-equipment dealers: plan changes and exit before signing
description: Understand why equipment inventory and dependence on a supplier can create duties beyond the brand agreement.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: This is not every service or equipment business
paragraphs: NRS 597.112–.118 concerns defined farm-equipment arrangements, including retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial supplier dependence. Inventory means the defined equipment, attachments or repair parts. A service brand or software licence does not qualify just because the contract says dealer.

sections.heading: Match the action to its conditions
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 generally requires good cause, 180 days’ written reasons before termination/nonrenewal and 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Listed grounds have different treatment; market-share failure has an assistance condition. Waiting alone does not prove cause.
Subsection (1) also requires good cause for a substantial agreement change, but the 180/60 provisions in (2)–(3) concern termination/nonrenewal, not every amendment.

Section 597.115(4) separately addresses action because of natural disaster, labour dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver/modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

sections.heading: Buyback needs item eligibility, not a stock total
paragraphs: Repurchase rules and exclusions depend on condition, age and other facts, including specified supplier-required systems/tools. Purchase and supplier-requirement records matter; gross stock or technology spending does not establish what must be repurchased.

practicalOutput: Identify coverage and whether the actual proposal is exit or substantial amendment before selecting notice or buyback assumptions.
limitations: Limited to defined farm-equipment dealers. Actual cause, exceptions and repurchase eligibility are not determined.
learningSummary: Nevada’s named farm-equipment dealer law can govern exit or major contract changes, but the 180-day notice is not a universal amendment rule. Establish its defined dealer relationship first.

title: New Hampshire chain-distributor review: participant payments and recruiting rights
description: Learn how to examine successive recruitment rights without assuming a master-operator title decides the legal result.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Trace what each participant buys and may recruit
paragraphs: RSA 358-B addresses participants investing and receiving rights to recruit others for economic gain, with those participants also investing and receiving recruiting rights. A master-franchise label, recruitment fee alone or genuine support work alone does not establish every element.

For example, a regional partner paid when operators join, where operators may buy rights to recruit further operators, needs the actual investments, rights and compensation source traced through each level. Separating customer-service revenue from joining/recruitment payments is an optional way to expose those facts, not a safe harbour.

sections.heading: A cap does not change a prohibited structure
paragraphs: The law says participant limits or eligibility conditions do not themselves change the identity of the defined scheme. Offering only ten regional territories therefore does not answer the test.

Where the prohibited device is established, the chapter prohibits promotion, offering or granting participation. Review the actual structure before recruitment, without treating every master or multi-level arrangement as unlawful.

practicalOutput: Clarify required investments, successive recruiting rights and compensation before promoting participation.
limitations: Only RSA 358-B’s specified branch is reviewed. Franchise disclosure, consumer, dealer and operating requirements remain separate and are not assumed absent.
learningSummary: A New Hampshire master-operator plan needs examination of required investments and successive recruiting rights—not just its territory count. Real support duties do not automatically resolve the defined chain-distributor test.
seoTitle: New Hampshire Chain-Distributor Plans: Payments and Rights

title: New Jersey office-based franchise coverage: the location and sales tests
description: A qualifying office can satisfy the location branch, but the general application route also has strict sales and franchise-share conditions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The Act has its own relationship definition
paragraphs: Section 56:10-3 requires the stated written arrangement for a definite or indefinite period, permission to use a trade name/mark/service mark or related characteristics, and a community of interest—the parties’ shared commercial interest—in marketing goods or services. A distribution label does not decide those facts.

For the place-of-business test, an office or warehouse is generally excluded. But for persons without a majority of sales directly to consumers, qualifying offices/warehouses from which personnel visit/call customers or goods are delivered can count. An address alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: For the general route, all three application criteria matter
paragraphs: Section 56:10-4(a) requires the following together for the franchisee, the operator receiving the rights. Section 4(b) has a separate new-motor-vehicle franchise route, not the same three-test rule.

rows: Performance contemplates or requires the franchisee to establish/maintain the defined location.
Covered product/service gross sales exceeded $35,000 during the twelve months immediately before suit is instituted.
More than 20% of the franchisee’s gross sales are intended to be or derived from the franchise.

sections.heading: Coverage is not a ruling on this operator
paragraphs: Section 56:10-8 excludes a franchise granted before the Act’s effective date, while renewal or amendment is not excluded on that basis. The source gives December 21, 1971 as the Act’s effective date.

The identified 2025 federal opinion considered pleaded allegations, not final factual findings about every distributor. Current definitions/application text is now readable, but this limited coverage guide does not supply the complete sector, case-law, filing, disclosure or exit analysis.

practicalOutput: Apply the actual relationship, location and sales facts to the correct route before relying on ongoing franchise protection.
limitations: Limited to the identified definitions, application criteria and prior-grant rule. Industry exceptions, complete case law and sales/exit procedures are not determined; the cited 2025 opinion tested allegations, not final facts.
learningSummary: A New Jersey office-based distributor can fall within the Franchise Practices Act, but office activity alone is not enough. Establish the written brand/community-of-interest relationship and the applicable combined criteria.

title: North Carolina business opportunities: check each promise separately
description: Understand why a U.S. trademark registration may answer one definition branch without removing other business-opportunity duties.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A mark is only one branch
paragraphs: Article 19 describes specified device-placement help, buying purchaser-produced products, income/refund promises and sales/marketing programs. Section 66-94(4)’s mark exception requires the stated U.S. federal registration; a home registration or pending application is not equivalent.

Ordinary customer-location help is not automatically the specified vending or similar-device placement. Section 66-94.1’s separate responsible-seller exemption has actual conditions and a sworn filing; reputation alone is insufficient.

For an actual income or refund promise, check whether the relevant provision requires a bond or trust, a form of financial protection. This is a conditional question, not a bond requirement for every offer.

sections.heading: If covered, file before the campaign
paragraphs: Section 66-97 requires filing before advertisements or other representations to prospective purchasers in the state, material-change updates and updates at least annually.

sections.heading: The buyer period is a different duty
paragraphs: Section 66-95 requires covered disclosure at least 48 hours before the earlier signature or receipt of consideration (money or other relevant value). A materially compliant federal Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD) is one permitted content route.
Using an FDD does not shorten the independently applicable federal fourteen-calendar-day period. Filing with the state and delivering to the buyer are different events.

practicalOutput: Separate each promise and establish the exact exclusion or exemption before advertising; if covered, meet filing and buyer delivery independently.
limitations: Limited to the stated business-opportunity branches. Actual mark/responsible-seller conditions and other sales or relationship requirements are not determined.
learningSummary: A federally registered mark can answer North Carolina’s specified marketing-program branch without removing a separate income guarantee or buyback trigger. Test the actual promise before treating the offer as excluded.

title: Ohio business opportunities: read what the exemption leaves in place
description: Understand why federal-compliant disclosure may remove many state duties while leaving security and buyback questions open.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The exemption leaves sections 1334.03(H) and 1334.04
paragraphs: Section 1334.13 removes most of the Business Opportunity Plans chapter for materially Federal Trade Commission (FTC)-compliant transactions, but expressly preserves these sections on payment/note security or buyback representations and related bond/trust duties.
Apply those surviving provisions to the actual equipment or protection promise; a compliant franchise disclosure package does not itself establish a bond or trust arrangement.

sections.heading: Ohio has its own definition and proof rules
paragraphs: Section 1334.01 uses supplied goods/services, payment conditions and specified representations. Its payment analysis is not the federal minimum-payment exemption.
Other exceptions appear in .12. In proceedings under .08 or .09, section .14 places the exemption/exception proof burden on the claimant.

sections.heading: The nonexempt buyer route is conditional
paragraphs: Covered nonexempt plans have disclosure, claim-substantiation, contract and cancellation provisions. The basic disclosure period is ten business days before agreement. The reviewed business-day definition excludes Sunday and legal holidays; a Monday–Friday calculator may be wrong.
Section 1334.05 cancellation is a separate conditional process, not a universal cancellation right for every franchise buyer. Independently applicable federal duties remain separate.

practicalOutput: Check any secured-payment or buyback promise against the surviving provisions even if the federal-compliance exemption otherwise applies.
limitations: The actual exemption, bond/trust and cancellation conditions are not decided. This is not complete Ohio franchise, dealer or operating coverage.

title: Oklahoma business opportunities and franchises: filing routes and advertising
description: Compare the 14-calendar-day exemption and qualified 15-full-business-day registration process. The current administrative advertising-filing rule remains unconfirmed.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Establish the particular exemption and state connections
paragraphs: The Act prohibits covered offers/sales without registration or exemption. Section 803(6) provides the stated business-opportunity/franchise route when the specified document is delivered fourteen calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration (money or other value).

Section 802 has its own business-opportunity, franchise and marketing-plan definitions, including relevant account-finding/training promises. The registered-mark/net-worth exclusion has further conditions. Section 805 puts proof of exemption/exclusion/exception on its claimant.

Section 818 separately examines offer origin/receipt, acceptance, domicile (the legally relevant home connection) and operating location. An outside outlet or internet format does not establish a blanket result for discovery calls or campaigns.

sections.heading: Registration effectiveness and advertising remain distinct

Sections 819–822 address fraud and misleading claims, including representing a filing as approval. The current administrative advertising-filing text could not be confirmed after agency-site failure; absence of a retrieved rule is not evidence of no advertising duty.

practicalOutput: Establish the exact exemption or complete registration route and resolve the current advertising rule before relying on a campaign timetable.
limitations: Actual definition, state connections and exemptions need application. The administrative advertising-filing rule remains unresolved.

title: Pennsylvania vehicle-dealer inventory buyback: return and payment events
description: Learn why the dealer’s product category, inventory records and tender date matter before using the 90-day and 60-day rules.

sections.heading: Section 316 is not a general franchise refund
paragraphs: The Board of Vehicles Act defines the dealer/franchise relationship and eligible inventory/equipment after specified termination or nonrenewal. Product category, condition, acquisition age and other limits matter, including particular treatment of motorcycle, recreational-vehicle and manufactured-housing arrangements.

A stock ledger or total startup spending does not establish eligibility. Vehicle identity/date/mileage/condition, parts, required tools/signs and ownership or creditor interests can matter to the actual item review; keeping those details is preparation, not expanded statutory coverage.

sections.heading: Separate the return event from tender
paragraphs: Apply section 316’s actual eligible-property and event conditions before calculating a deadline.

title: South Carolina business opportunities: organise the promises before the campaign
description: Learn why mark registration, filing, earnings evidence and buyer disclosure answer different questions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The mark exception is limited
paragraphs: Section 39-57-20 has specified business-startup arrangements and representations. The registered-mark exception sits within its sales/marketing-program branch; device-placement assistance, purchasing buyer-made products and guarantee/refund promises have their own terms.

Apply the fee condition and other exclusions too. Ordinary customer-finding is not automatically vending-device placement. A cleaning support offer with a startup refund needs that actual refund promise tested separately, including unresolved financial-protection conditions.

sections.heading: Covered promotion needs filing and claims support
paragraphs: Section 39-57-50 requires filing before advertisements or other representations, use of the assigned registration number in promotion, material-change updates and updates at least biennially (once every two years). A filing number is not endorsement; statements about state compliance have separate limits.
Section 39-57-60(1) requires documented evidence supporting the earnings claim to be disclosed when the representation is made. Internal possession of a spreadsheet is not that disclosure.

Section 39-57-30 separately requires disclosure 48 hours before the earlier business-opportunity contract or consideration (money or other value). Independently applicable federal disclosure is not shortened.

practicalOutput: Separate the actual marketing, refund and income promises before promotion; if covered, complete filing and provide the required claim evidence and buyer disclosure.
limitations: Limited to the stated business-opportunity branches. Actual fees, representations, exclusions and financial-protection conditions are not determined.
learningSummary: South Carolina examines the actual startup promises, not only the brand’s registration. A refund or earnings promise can raise a different definition branch from the marketing program.

title: Tennessee franchise tax is not franchise-sales permission
description: Understand the limited distinction between Tennessee franchise-and-excise tax questions and franchise sales. The 2021 FAQs do not settle current tax or state franchise-law duties.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Federal disregarded status does not finish state tax
paragraphs: Revenue’s F&E-1 FAQ lists corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs) and other entity types that may have return obligations. F&E-4 explains that a federally disregarded LLC—ignored as a separate entity for the relevant federal tax purpose—can still need a Tennessee return unless an exemption applies.

These FAQs are dated March 2021. The actual taxpayer, federal classification, Tennessee activities/connections, tax year, current law and exemption conditions still need examination. They are not a complete current calculation or filing calendar.

A Singapore parent, U.S. LLC and Tennessee operator can therefore have different factual roles. Completing the LLC’s tax account does not resolve the separate brand-rights, fee, control and support arrangement.

sections.heading: Current franchise-sales rules remain unresolved
paragraphs: The June 2021 consumer-agency help explanation identifies its consumer-protection role, not current franchise statutory requirements. Attempts to retrieve the linked code and court text did not provide usable legal bodies.
State offer/sale filings, exemptions, advertising and relationship rules are not established here. Failed access is not proof of no duty; independently applicable federal disclosure remains separate.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual taxpayer and current tax-year questions without treating a tax account as permission to sell franchise rights.
limitations: Limited to the tax-versus-sales distinction from dated FAQs. Current tax scope and Tennessee franchise-law coverage remain unresolved.
learningSummary: Tennessee franchise tax and selling a franchise are different subjects. The cited Revenue FAQs identify entity-tax questions; they do not establish permission to recruit a branded operator.

title: Utah franchise notices: obtain the receipt before the covered offer
description: Learn the current receipt, renewal and information-update rules without confusing notice with buyer disclosure.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The trigger includes Utah residents
paragraphs: Section 13-15-201(2) addresses a franchise to be located in Utah or offered/sold to a Utah resident. An out-of-state outlet does not remove the resident branch.

The notice states substantial federal Franchise Rule compliance and includes the required applicant, brand, address and public identification information. The actual seller and qualifying conditions still matter.

sections.heading: Three dates under the section effective May 6, 2026

rows: Valid for one year from issue.
Compliance at least 30 days before expiry.
Update within 30 days of that event, not just at annual renewal.

sections.heading: The general business-opportunity route differs
paragraphs: Section 201(2)(c) directs those not qualifying for the franchise notice to subsection (1), with its own disclosure content and ten-business-day purchaser-delivery provisions.
Neither receipt is state approval. Independently applicable federal FDD (Franchise Disclosure Document) delivery remains separate from the Utah receipt.

practicalOutput: Establish the qualifying route and obtain proof of notice receipt before the covered offer; use issue and information-change dates for their separate duties.
limitations: Actual seller, resident/location facts and compliance conditions are not determined. This does not complete every filing, disclosure or operating requirement.
learningSummary: On Utah’s qualifying franchise route, proof of the issued notice receipt must precede the covered offer or sale. A prepared notice or completed disclosure document is not that receipt.

title: Vermont equipment partners: choose the right exit process before using a deadline
description: Learn how product definitions, termination reasons and inventory records shape a covered dealership exit.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Check products and dealer status
paragraphs: Title 9, Chapter 107 has dealer and inventory definitions and can cover oral/written agreements. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line category are excluded.
Adding utility-equipment sales/repairs to a service offer raises a different question from the brand licence alone. Describe the actual equipment relationship before selecting an exit branch.

sections.heading: Use the process for the actual ground
paragraphs: Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day opportunity to correct the stated problem. Market-penetration termination has a separate initial 24-month period and final-notice process. Specified events allow immediate termination. The special market-penetration and immediate-event procedures are not fully set out here.
An alleged performance problem does not establish cause or a listed immediate event. Do not substitute the general period for the actual market-penetration requirements.

sections.heading: Stock value is not a repurchase claim
paragraphs: Sections 4073–4074 make repurchase subject to request, item eligibility, valuation and payment requirements. Source, age, condition, title and the actual request matter; the total inventory account is not an automatic reimbursement.

practicalOutput: Confirm coverage and the actual exit ground, then apply its notice/correction process and item-specific repurchase conditions separately.
limitations: Limited to the named equipment-dealer branch. Actual exclusions, cause, immediate-event and repurchase conditions are not determined.
learningSummary: Vermont’s equipment-dealer exit rules depend on the defined products and the reason for ending the arrangement. A general 120-day notice is not the process for every event.

title: West Virginia equipment dealers: map inventory, repairs and the exit process
description: Learn why the dealer definition and item records matter before applying the six-month termination rule or estimating repurchase.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Check retail sales, inventory and repairs
paragraphs: Coverage includes the stated retail sellers and inventory/repair-service conditions. A service licence alone does not establish it, and industrial rather than farm use does not automatically exclude it.

sections.heading: Apply the stated service, contents and exception conditions
paragraphs: Section 47-11F-3 generally requires six months’ termination notice, prescribed written service and contents. Listed exceptions and the mutual-consent route need separate application.
A contract clause or ordinary message does not establish the statutory procedure. Keep the period as six months rather than converting it to a fixed day count.

sections.heading: Value, return and payment are different questions
paragraphs: Sections 4–5 govern conditional inventory repurchase, including valuation, timing and exclusions. Source, age, condition, title and current-net-price evidence matter; a retail price or gross stock balance is not automatically the statutory value.
Track actual termination, physical return and payment separately, including responsible payer and unresolved warranty questions. Budgeting possible exposure does not establish entitlement.

practicalOutput: Establish dealer coverage, then apply the actual notice procedure and item-specific return/payment conditions.
limitations: Limited to the named equipment branch. Definitions, notice exceptions, mutual-consent and repurchase conditions are not determined for an actual arrangement.
learningSummary: West Virginia’s Farm Equipment Dealer Contract Act can include specified construction, industrial and outdoor-power sellers. If covered, its six-month notice is a prescribed procedure—not an assumed number of days or an informal email.

title: Wyoming equipment dealers: identify the notice regime before ending the agreement
description: Learn why general and single-line dealer branches have different notice periods and why inventory has its own review.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with equipment and granted rights
paragraphs: Chapter 40-20 covers defined equipment dealers/suppliers, including specified industrial, maintenance, utility and grounds-care equipment. Actual products, sale/repair rights, agreement, exclusions and single-line conditions matter; using equipment or one brand does not itself settle them.

sections.heading: The two ordinary tracks
paragraphs: Specified events and performance failures have different conditions; actual reasons, comparable standards and improvement history remain necessary.

rows: 180 days’ notice, sixty days to cure.
Ninety days’ notice, sixty days to cure.

sections.heading: Notice does not decide buyback or succession
paragraphs: Sections 120–121 have separate repurchase duties/exclusions. Actual property source, dates, condition, return and payment conditions determine item treatment; not every startup cost is recoverable.
Use the inventory companion for those details. Any succession request also needs its actual facts rather than an answer copied from the termination calendar.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual dealer category and proposed action before selecting the notice branch; assess inventory and succession independently.
limitations: Limited to the defined equipment branch, not a general Wyoming franchise exit rule. Actual performance, exception and category conditions remain necessary.
learningSummary: Wyoming’s ordinary equipment-dealer notice differs for the general and single-line branches. You must establish the actual category before choosing 180 or 90 days; neither is automatic exit permission. This page compares the ordinary tracks; it does not supply the full single-line eligibility or special-event/performance tests.

title: D.C. Basic Business License versus company and premises permissions
description: Consumer-protection rules and the steps to obtain a local business licence answer different questions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What does “all permissions included” cover?
paragraphs: The Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection separates corporate/trade-name registration, tax registration, zoning or home-occupation/occupancy requirements, and the activity-based Basic Business License application.

If a training brand promises all permissions are included, identify the actual holder, activity and address of each permission. A licence held by the brand may not establish the operator’s own required permission; company registration does not settle use of the proposed premises.
An operating licence also does not establish franchise disclosure compliance. This page has not completed the D.C. franchise-sales requirements.

sections.heading: The sales-claim law has its own coverage
paragraphs: Section 28-3901 includes franchises/business opportunities in its goods/services definition but separately defines consumer, merchant and transaction. That inclusion does not decide every business-to-business purchase.

Section 28-3904 addresses covered material misstatements and omissions. Actual buyer, purpose, seller and transaction facts and current application notes matter; do not assume every printed change has the same implemented effect or every broad pitch has the same legal result.

practicalOutput: Before promising all permissions, check what each actual operator and address still needs and make the sales statement match those facts.
limitations: Consumer Protection Procedures Act coverage is not established for every B2B operator. This is not a completed activity-specific licence or premises review, and franchise-sales questions remain unresolved.
learningSummary: A D.C. brand’s operating permission does not automatically cover a new operator or its premises. Corporate records, tax registration, premises permissions and the activity-based Basic Business License answer different questions.
